protocol.core_question: Can compact, incremental notes preserve answer quality and event changes while reducing earlier and request-time token cost?
protocol.note_schedule: Reuse the frozen 25–40 second chunk boundaries (requested range 10–40 seconds); new transcript since the previous query plus up to ten seconds of earlier reference context.
protocol.snapshot: One replacement state, at most sixteen facts and eight explicit changes.
protocol.delta: At most six source-supported add/update/retire edits; program keeps sixteen active notes, the latest eight changes in model input and the full version archive on disk.
protocol.primary_reader_input: Full transcript plus a single current note state; old-all and old-latest controls reuse the original generated snapshots.
protocol.legacy_cost: Count saved structured-note generation once per meeting; no note generation is charged to reactive; old-latest shares the complete historical generation cost with old-all.
protocol.selection_rule: Review development accuracy, change retention, duplication, malformed edits and total cost; freeze a selected policy before additional-meeting or generated-transcript tests.
protocol.next_stage: Evaluate a frozen policy on at least twelve additional questions from at least six meetings, including reactive baselines; then automatic Parakeet/Whisper on the six existing questions.
protocol.evaluation: Codex compares final answers with source-reviewed required facts and original evidence; parse success is separate from answer correctness. Check every development answer and every changed/unsupported held-out answer. Report fact correctness plus unsupported claims, not citation presence alone.
protocol.change_audit: Inspect actual deadline/owner/decision revisions, source support and unresolved-state retention; check exact and near duplicate notes and low-information entries.

roles.0: Pinned text model weights plus 8 GiB KV cache; vLLM graphs and prefix caching; writer then reader

resources.shared_components: No S1, TTS or ASR services; writer and reader share the same model sequentially.
resources.dependencies: The two development model jobs are independent; later runs depend on content review and a frozen selection.

literature.instruction: Optimize structured notes for token efficiency, low duplication/noise and conversation event changes.
literature.scope: Question-blind incremental meeting notes for the existing AMI text S2 readers.
sub_questions: Which facts merit storage before the question is known?
How should a current fact be updated without erasing its prior state?
How much cost comes from repeated snapshots and repeated transcript reading?
Do smaller notes preserve source-complete answers and lower request-time reasoning?
literature.search_scope: Nine papers; more than five distinct search formulations; primary sources verified; recent papers are separated from peer-reviewed work.

papers.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.authors: Prateek Chhikara, Dev Khant, Saket Aryan, Taranjeet Singh, Deshraj Yadav
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Separate fact extraction from ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP memory operations using related existing memories.
papers.results: Authors report better LoCoMo accuracy and substantially lower token/latency costs than their full-context comparison.
papers.relevance: Use edits and explicit no-change output; preserve old versions instead of deleting revision evidence.

papers.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Wujiang Xu, Zujie Liang, Kai Mei, Hang Gao, Juntao Tan, Yongfeng Zhang
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Create atomic structured notes and link related memories; new evidence can update older note context.
papers.results: Evaluations over six foundation models report gains from memory linking and evolution.
papers.relevance: Use stable event IDs and explicit relationships; avoid copying keywords/tags that add cost without a tested benefit.

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.authors: Di Wu, Hongwei Wang, Wenhao Yu, Yuwei Zhang, Kai-Wei Chang, Dong Yu
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Evaluate extraction, cross-session reasoning, time, knowledge updates and unanswered questions; separate indexing, retrieval and reading.
papers.results: The 500-question benchmark exposes long-history forgetting; decomposition and time-aware retrieval improve recall.
papers.relevance: Score updates, ownership and uncertainty separately; a correct current state must not erase a relevant old state.

papers.title: Recursively Summarizing Enables Long-Term Dialogue Memory in Large Language Models
papers.authors: Qingyue Wang, Yanhe Fu, Yanan Cao, Shuai Wang, Zhiliang Tian, Liang Ding
papers.venue: Neurocomputing (acceptance stated on arXiv; bibliographic publication year not inferred)
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Generate a new compact memory from the previous memory and new dialogue, then use the latest memory.
papers.results: Reported dialogue consistency gains with open and closed models; this does not guarantee lossless fact retention.
papers.relevance: A latest-state replacement is an important simple control against accumulated snapshots.

papers.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
papers.authors: Zijian Zhou, Ao Qu, Zhaoxuan Wu, Sunghwan Kim, Alok Prakash, Daniela Rus, Jinhua Zhao, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Paul Pu Liang
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Train a recurrent compact memory state with reinforcement learning rather than retaining the entire interaction.
papers.results: Reports improved long-horizon task performance and smaller memory; requires training rather than prompting alone.
papers.relevance: Motivates bounded current memory; the present pilot tests prompts without claiming to reproduce trained MEM1.

papers.title: SimpleMem: Efficient Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Jiaqi Liu, Yaofeng Su, Peng Xia, Siwei Han, Zeyu Zheng, Cihang Xie, Mingyu Ding, Huaxiu Yao
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Filter low-information turns, extract self-contained facts, consolidate related content and retrieve according to the question.
papers.results: Authors report improved LoCoMo F1 and lower inference tokens; exact gains depend on their retrieval-based setup.
papers.relevance: Filter fillers and redundant confirmations, but keep short rejections that change decisions; preserve relative times when AMI has no calendar date.

papers.title: AriadneMem: Threading the Maze of Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Use information filtering and conflict-aware consolidation, preserving state transitions as temporal links.
papers.results: Abstract reports stronger multi-hop F1 and lower runtime on LoCoMo; full experimental reproduction is outside this review.
papers.relevance: Keep a compact change log alongside current facts; similarity alone must not merge different event states.

papers.title: MemSIF: From Structured Interactions to Dual-Track Fact Memory for LLM Agents
papers.authors: YuFei Luo, Xiucheng Xu, Zhen Yang
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Group coherent topical segments and link nonadjacent segments belonging to an evolving event; distinguish stable facts from facts formed on demand.
papers.results: Reports gains on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S across five LLMs; no direct AMI/streaming evidence.
papers.relevance: Use an event/topic ID for updates across separated chunks; question-blind salience is uncertain, so retain the original full transcript at answer time.

papers.title: LeanMem: Simple and Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Yuxin Liao, Le Wu, Min Hou, Hao Liu, Han Wu, Zishu Wang
papers.verification: Opened primary arXiv abstract; method details checked in available primary HTML for Mem0, A-MEM, MemSIF, SimpleMem, LeanMem and MEM1.
papers.problem: Efficient, reliable long-conversation memory with evolving facts.
papers.method: Treat stable profiles, changing events and source-grounded records differently; selectively update dynamic event memories.
papers.results: Reports accuracy and construction-cost gains on LoCoMo/LongMemEval-S; independent meeting results remain untested.
papers.relevance: Update only affected notes, keep source IDs for exact quantities and decisions, and measure construction cost separately from request cost.

themes: Maintain a current state with explicit updates instead of appending full repeated snapshots.
Separate stable facts, current event state and revision evidence.
Store sources and uncertain states; compression can erase useful qualifiers.
Evaluate construction, retrieval and answering separately.

gaps.statement: Most reported token savings compare retrieved memory with full-history inputs; they do not directly establish lower native request thinking when the full transcript is retained.
Stable speaker ownership, disfluent speech and unresolved AMI discussion require source checks beyond schema validity.
gaps.evidence: Current AMI source reviews and longmemeval update/abstention categories.

gaps.statement: A prompt-only incremental edit system may reduce copying but still merge distinct events or mistake intent for completion.
gaps.evidence: memsif event linking, ariadne state transitions; present hypotheses require experiments.
